messages:
Marta: Quick sync — I'm proposing a concise mapping for client errors so SDKs and the console can be consistent.
Marta: Goal: separate transient throttles (retryable) from quota/billing (actionable in console) and give observability labels we can use for rollouts.
Ryan: Sounds good. Can you sketch the HTTP mapping you have in mind? SDKs currently treat 429 as "retryable" by default.
Marta: Draft mapping:
- 429 = transient rate-limit (burst); includes Retry-After and subcode like rate_limit.per_minute
- 503 = soft backpressure / runtime overload (not client traffic shaped) — returns x-runtime-throttle hint
- 403 = quota_exceeded (billing or tenant quota) — non-retryable, contains quota_reset and console link
Marta: Example error body for quota_exceeded (console can link directly):
```
{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "message": "Monthly request quota reached for org AcmeCorp",
  "quota_reset_at": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "console_link": "https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/AcmeCorp/usage"
}
```
Kevin: I like separating quota from retry. One ask: many clients treat any 4xx as non-retryable; SDKs will need a small bump to check error.error and allow retries on 429 only.
Ryan: Agreed. We'll update client-side logic to: if status==429 -> retry policy; if status==503 -> exponential backoff; if status==403 && error=="quota_exceeded" -> no retry, surface console link and billing contact.
Sara: Telemetry needs: error_category, throttle_class, and quota_bucket. Suggested metric labels:
```
api.request.error_count{error_category="quota_exceeded|rate_limit|backpressure", throttle_class="per_minute|per_day|runtime", quota_bucket="monthly_api_calls"}
```
Sara: Also add a trace tag `client.visible_error` so the console can correlate sessions -> support tickets easily.
Marta: UX: console badge colors: blue=informational (near quota), yellow=approaching, red=blocked. Show suggested mitigation (upgrade, reduce tokens, batched requests) and a one-click link to request a quota increase.
Kevin: For rollout: canary 5% of traffic to new mapping; track two KPIs: a) spike in "unexpected_retries" (clients retrying 403), b) support ticket rate referencing 'quota_exceeded'. If either increases > 50% we abort.
Ryan: Telemetry sample event for canary:
```
{ "event": "client_error_exposed", "status": 403, "error": "quota_exceeded", "canary_group": "v2-mapping" }
```
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary start @ 2026-03-25T14:00Z -> 5% for 2h, auto-increase to 25% if KPIs stable. See: https://deploys.redwood.ai/rollouts/3065403210
Marta: Nice. Action items:
- Ryan: PR to SDKs to distinguish 429 vs 403 quota_exceeded (small change, toggle behind flag)
- Kevin: add console CTA + badge states to the usage page
- Sara: add metric labels and example dashboards for canary monitoring
- Ops: run canary as deploy-bot scheduled
Ryan: Will open PR today and include a migration guide for integrators.
Kevin: I'll stub the console CTA and a mockup in Figma, pinging design.
Sara: I'll add dashboards and an alert that fires if support tickets with "quota_exceeded" > baseline +50% during canary.
Marta: Thanks all. If no objections, we'll start the deploy-bot job and monitor the KPIs. :thumbsup:
